newsitem.title: BRAZIL: HSBC Brazil deal involves 5.7 bln reais in credit.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Brazil deal involves 5.7 bln reais in credit.

text.p: The takeover of failed Brazilian bank Bamerindus by the Hong Kong & Shanghai Banking Corp will involve a total of 5.7 billion reais in various credit lines, Central Bank officials said.
Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said 2.5 billion reais in special PROER credit would be passed to the federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal to assume Bamerindus' mortgage portfolio.
Another 300 million reais would be passed to state-owned Banco do Brasil to liquidate international operations assumed by the Banco do Brasil.
The takeover by the Central Bank of the old Bamerindus will itself involve 2.5 billion reais in funds from the FGC deposit guaratee fund, which covers deposits of up to 20,000 reais per investor.
Finally, another credit line of 400 million reais would be used to cover debt to the Central Bank which had been guaranteed by federal securities.
Central Bank director of controls Claudio Mauch said that, in total, some 850 million reais would end up back with the Central Bank.
Loyola stressed that few of the credits involved public funds. He said the 2.5 billion reais of FGC funds were deposits made by banks themselves.

"This is being paid by the banking system itself to help one of its own," Loyola said. He added that the money for the Banco do Brasil and the Caixa Economica Federal was public money going into public banks, with "no credit risk."
